fable.w: This section only authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to acquire real property and carry out military construction projects at listed installations in specified amounts. The tempting reading is that acquiring real property involves outside landowners or states, but the text provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Navy may acquire real property and carry out military construction projects for the installations or locations inside the United States

opus.w: This section lets the Secretary of the Navy buy land and carry out construction projects at listed locations for set dollar amounts. It has no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving outside parties. The states named in the tables only say where the projects are; nothing gives those states a role in deciding anything.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Navy may acquire real property and carry out military construction projects for the installations or locations inside the United States, and in the amounts, set forth in the following table
opus.b: The only possible trap is that this section authorizes federal decisions about buying land and running construction projects at named locations, including in states. But it never requires or allows anyone outside the federal government to take part in those decisions. It is purely a funding and project authorization for the Secretary of the Navy.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to spend appropriated funds on military construction at specified locations. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties such as state or local governments, the public, or private entities. The decision-making process is internal to the federal executive branch.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the Navy may acquire real property and carry out military construction projects for the installations or locations inside the United States, and in the amounts, set forth in the following table
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the construction projects are located in specific states (e.g., Arizona, California), the state governments or local communities are implicitly involved or consulted. However, the text only lists locations and funding amounts; it does not mandate any consultation, coordination, or participation by state or local entities. The decision-making authority rests entirely with the Secretary of the Navy.
